$comment: Reference schema for one entry in data/recipes.json. Not machine-validated — used as a template/reminder when writing new recipes.
name: Human-readable recipe name — succinct, no appliance/size/parenthetical annotations (e.g. no '(5L Ninja Foodi)' or '(6L)'); if the dish is a recognisable regional style (Indian, Thai, Mexican, etc.), name that cuisine in the title
source: Short provenance note, e.g. 'Generated with Claude — Ninja Foodi example recipe'
base_servings: number — how many servings the base_qty amounts below are written for
cook_method: e.g. 'Ninja Foodi — Sear/Sauté then Pressure Cook'
estimated_volume_l: number — estimated total pot volume at base_servings; keep <= 4 for legumes/rice/grains under pressure, <= 3 for very foamy foods, always < 6

ingredients.name: ingredient description as it should read in a recipe/ingredient list
ingredients.base_qty: plain number at base_servings, e.g. 800 or 2 or 0.5 (no fractions/ranges)
ingredients.category: one of the Australian grocery aisle categories in references/coles_aisles.md
ingredients.product: a specific, realistic product name/size you'd find at an Australian grocer like Coles (sourcing reference: references/coles_aisles.md) — but don't brand it as 'Coles X'; use the plain product name for store-brand items (e.g. 'Brown Onions', not 'Coles Brown Onions') and real third-party brand names where genuinely a branded product (e.g. 'SunRice Basmati Rice 1kg', 'Massel Salt Reduced Chicken Style Liquid Stock 1L') — the site/shopping list never mentions Coles by name
ingredients.discrete: optional boolean — true for items bought as whole units (cans, onions, garlic bulbs, limes, bunches) so shopping-list scaling rounds up instead of scaling fractionally

method: Ordered array of Ninja Foodi steps as strings, naming the actual function used (Sear/Sauté, Pressure Cook, Air Fry Crisp, Slow Cook, Steam). Fold any need-to-know technique detail (e.g. 'don't boil hard once the yoghurt is in, or it may split') directly into the relevant step rather than a separate notes field — recipe pages show only ingredients and method, no extra commentary.
